clock_quality.rule: exact: our own live capture, available_utc equals captured_utc; published: an agency vintage (ALFRED, FOMC statement) or provider actual/previous/revision whose availability is the scheduled release instant in available_utc, null when only the day (available_date) is known; unvintaged: a consensus read from a calendar after the event, available_utc set to the capture time, never before the release

columns.meaning: which figure of the release: nfp_change, cpi_mom, ism_mfg_pmi, fed_funds_upper, ...
columns.name: measure

columns.meaning: period the figure covers (YYYY-MM, YYYY-Qn, week-ending date, FOMC meeting label)
columns.name: period_ref

columns.meaning: K thousands, M millions, % percent, index points
columns.name: unit

columns.meaning: endpoint or page the row came from (credentials redacted)
columns.name: source_url

columns.meaning: when we fetched the bytes the row was parsed from
columns.name: captured_utc

columns.meaning: when the value became available: exact = captured_utc; published = the scheduled release instant; null when only the day is known
columns.name: available_utc

columns.meaning: civil day the value became available (always set)
columns.name: available_date

columns.meaning: exact | published | unvintaged (see README.md, Clock quality)
columns.name: clock_quality

columns.meaning: raw capture under build/calendar/ listed in raw/INDEX.csv
columns.name: capture_path

notes.units: one registered unit per measure (swing_dataset.calendar.units.MEASURE_UNITS); each source declares the unit its own numbers are in and is converted onto that unit before the row is built; the build fails if a row leaves it or if two sources of the same actual disagree by more than 5.0x over 4 or more shared periods
